title: KV ternary/FP8 hybrid staging probe for progressive fidelity gating
creator: Priya Desai
description: Purpose: Probe a hybrid KV cache compression strategy that interleaves aggressive low-bit encodings (ternary and INT4) for cold/low-importance keys with FP8 for recently accessed or high-fidelity regions, combined with a progressive fidelity gating policy driven by request cohort signals. Goal is to reduce GPU KV memory pressure by >=35% on tail-heavy production traces while keeping end-user quality regressions within an acceptable band (≤1.5% relative loss on evaluated generation metrics) and maintaining latency SLOs for P95 tokens. Motivation: Prior KV quant experiments (INT8/INT4/FP8) show varied degradation patterns across workloads and prompt cohorts. We want a practical runtime-first approach that: a) dynamically moves hot keys to higher-fidelity encodings, b) stores long-tail keys in ultra-compact formats (ternary/INT4), and c) offers deterministic fallbacks to full-precision shards for safety-critical customers.
experiment_plan: Design hybrid encoding format: per-kv-shard metadata indicates encoding depth (ternary / INT4 / INT8 / FP8 / full FP16), recency score, and cohort tag.
Implement on-runtime prototype: encode/decode paths for ternary (2-bit+sign packing), block-wise INT4, and NVIDIA-style FP8 (e4m3/e5m2) using our kernel selection layer.

Workload selection: run on two production-derived traces (chat-heavy conversational trace and long-document summarization trace) plus an adversarial synthetic set with rare tokens and long context stretches.

Metrics to capture: GPU KV memory footprint, token-level latency (P50/P95/P99), throughput (tokens/sec), model quality (perplexity delta, ROUGE-L for summarization, empiric response bias checks), error rates for fallback events, and incidence of divergence in deterministic tests.

Progressive fidelity gating policy: compute per-key score = alpha*recency + beta*cohort_importance + gamma*token_entropy; thresholding moves keys between encodings at runtime; knobs exposed via config.

Safety fallback: on top-k likelihood drop detected (>2% lift in perplexity for a prompt cohort) trigger synchronous restore to FP16 for affected keys for that request; record and expose reasons in tracing headers.

Phases: Phase A (lab offline sweep to map quality vs memory curves), Phase B (shadow traffic on a small percentage of production requests), Phase C (canary with limited write-through to active cache), Phase D (rollout or rollback).
acceptance_criteria: Average KV memory reduction ≥ 35% on target traces in Phase B compared to baseline FP16 cache
End-user quality regression ≤ 1.5% relative loss on task metrics (perplexity for LM tasks; ROUGE/ROUGE-L for summarization) across cohorts designated as "guarded"
No more than 0.5% of requests should observe synchronous fallback events that add >10ms tail latency
P95 token latency remains within current SLO +5ms under baseline batching distributions
All fallback events and encoding transitions must be traceable in the Console rollout dashboard for debugging
instrumentation: Telemetry: per-request trace tags (encoding snapshot for keys read, recency scores, fallback triggers)
Dashboards: KV memory heatmap, encoding churn rate, fallback event timeline, cohort-specific quality deltas
Automated test harness: deterministic seeds for generation, golden outputs to detect bit-exact regressions when using FP16 fallback
Benchmarks: microbench for encode/decode throughput and latency per shard size on A100 and H100
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Ternary/INT4 quantization causes catastrophic tail-case degradation for rare token sequences. Mitigation: conservative gating for keys with low token entropy and immediate FP16 fallback path plus offline artifact that enumerates high-risk n-grams.

Risk: Encoding/decoding CPU overhead increases per-request latency. Mitigation: implement async background encode tasks, prefetch hot-key decodes into faster per-GPU caches, and measure CPU overhead in Phase A.
Risk: Increased memory fragmentation from mixed encodings. Mitigation: slab allocator with compaction window during low load and metadata-level compaction signals.
Risk: Hard-to-debug model drift when hybrid policy changes behavior. Mitigation: strict rollouts, per-cohort canarying, and automated regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals in Redwood Optimize
test_results_summary: Phase A lab sweep (2026-03-05): On conversational trace, FP8-only reduced KV memory by ~28% with median perplexity delta +0.9%; INT4-only reduced memory by ~42% but produced higher perplexity delta +3.4% and occasional hallucination patterns on rare-token prompts. Hybrid policy (ternary for tail, FP8 for recent hot keys) achieved ~36% memory reduction with perplexity delta +1.2% and fewer hallucination signatures vs INT4-only. Microbench: ternary encode/decode adds 0.6ms per shard on average; FP8 paths show ~10% faster decode than FP16. Observed encoding churn (hotness flips) at default gating parameters causes ~2% extra writes; tune alpha/beta to stabilize. These are preliminary lab results; Phase B shadow runs scheduled next week.
decisions: Proceed with hybrid ternary+FP8 prototype into Phase B shadowing (approved by runtime-ops and models).
Default gating parameters: alpha(recency)=0.6, beta(cohort_importance)=0.3, gamma(entropy)=0.1; will be exposed as a per-deployment config.
Fallback policy: synchronous FP16 restore per-request when cohort-level quality delta crosses configured threshold; asynchronous background re-encode after quality stabilizes.
We will not enable INT4-only on production caches without additional cohort-level safety nets and longer shadowing (deferred).
next_steps: Instrument shadow traffic with full tracing and run Phase B for two weeks on 1% of production traffic (start 2026-03-12).
Add automated golden-seed checks for 200 canonical prompts each for conversational and summarization cohorts.
Tune gating parameters to reduce encoding churn to <1% write overhead based on initial shadow telemetry.
Create a lightweight console widget to visualize per-deployment fidelity distributions and recent fallback events for SREs and customers.
